title: Compact graphs and quantum automorphisms
authors: Pedro Baptista, Gabriel Coutinho, Chris Godsil, Simon Schmidt
abstract: Compact graphs are graphs for which the fractional automorphism polytope has no genuinely fractional vertices. This paper proposes a quantum analogue of this idea by evaluating the fundamental magic unitary of the quantum automorphism group on states, which we show to produce a closed convex set of doubly stochastic matrices sitting between the classical automorphism polytope and the full fractional automorphism polytope. Our main result is that the natural quantum analogue of compactness is classical, that is, a quantum compact graph is classically compact.   We also relate this set to the quantum orbital algebra and obtain a hierarchy of classical and quantum compactness pseudo notions. The framework recovers familiar consequences of compactness through commutants and suggests quantum analogues of generous transitivity and distance-transitivity. We also isolate examples and open problems indicating where quantum symmetries may strictly refine the classical compactness theory.
summary: This theoretical paper explores a quantum generalization of 'compact graphs' by examining the relationship between classical and quantum automorphism structures. The core finding is that any graph satisfying the quantum definition of compactness must also satisfy the stricter, classical definition. This establishes a deep connection between algebraic symmetry theory and geometric properties of graphs.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a quantum analogue of 'compact graphs,' which are classically defined by properties of their fractional automorphism polytope, and determine if this quantum notion is equivalent to the classical one.
main_result: The natural quantum analogue of compactness is shown to be classical: if the set of quantum fractional automorphisms equals the full fractional automorphism polytope, then the graph must also satisfy the condition for classical compactness.
method: The authors use techniques from $	ext{C}^*$-algebras and state space analysis on the quantum automorphism group algebra to define and analyze sets like the quantum fractional automorphism polytope ($	ext{QP}(A)$).
model_or_system: The system under study is an abstract graph $X$ and its associated symmetry structures, including the classical and quantum orbital algebras derived from its automorphism groups.
key_observables: Quantum fractional automorphism set ($	ext{QP}(A)$), Classical/Fractional Automorphism Polytopes ($P(A)$, $S(A)$), Quantum Orbital Algebra ($	ext{QO}(X)$).
important_parameters: Graph structure (e.g., regularity, distance-regularity) and the fundamental magic unitary defining the quantum symmetries.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing inclusions between various matrix algebras derived from the automorphism group representations.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes; the focus is on algebraic relationships and set inclusions (e.g., $P(A) \subseteq QP(A) \subseteq S(A)$).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining quantum analogues of classical graph properties, establishing key structural theorems relating these sets ($	ext{QP}(A)$ is closed/convex), and culminating in the main result that quantum compactness implies classical compactness.
why_interesting: While not directly about AMO systems, the rigorous mathematical framework developed for analyzing symmetries (automorphism groups) using $	ext{C}^*$-algebras and state spaces provides powerful tools applicable to understanding symmetry breaking or structure preservation in complex quantum many-body models.
